newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CCB issue price max 2,675 bfr - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CCB issue price max 2,675 bfr - paper.

text.p: Belgian bank Credit Communal de Belgique/Gemeentekrediet (CCB), which is owned by local authorities, will be bourse listed at a maximum price of 2,675 francs per share, Belgian financial dailies L'Echo and De Financieel-Economische Tijd said on Friday.
The 30 billion franc initial public offering of up to 29.5 percent of the bank's shares opens for retail investors today and will close on November 15.
The bank is expected to set an indicative issue price today. The final price of the IPO will be fixed on November 20, when the stock will first be traded.
A spokesman for CCB confirmed the issue price which was published in advertisements in the papers.
Subscriptions for professional investors opened on November 4.

The bourse listing is part of CCB's alliance with French Credit Local de France. CCB and CLF plan to join forces to create Europe's 22nd largest banking group, which will operate internationally under the brand name DEXIA.
CCB has applied to the Brussels Stock Exchange to be listed under the name DEXIA-CC.
